summary: Settlement posting stopped because order-service v2.16.0 (dep-6010, 07:40:00Z) began emitting OrderExecuted events in a v2 schema (field renamed qty->quantity, new 'venue' field, v2 schema-version header) that settlement-service's v1 deserializer cannot parse; the first failure is at 07:42:14Z, 2m14s after the deploy. The consumer treats the record at orders-3@8841207 as a poison message and retries the same offset in a tight loop (tens of thousands of attempts), pinning CPU ~70% and blocking the partition, so request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s and consumer lag climbs monotonically to ~60k. The reporter's suspected config change (cfg-3004, max.poll.records 500->200) is refuted on mechanism — a batch-size parameter cannot produce a deserialization error or a partition-blocked spin. Confidence is medium (0.69): every obtainable discriminator (tight timing, change-content match, blast radius confined to the one v1 decoder, flat kafka partition health, refuted alternatives) points to this cause, but the producer-side wire artifact was never directly observed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 emits v2-schema OrderExecuted events that settlement-service cannot deserialize, blocking the orders-3 partition
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, 07:40Z) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity, added 'venue', and set a v2 schema-version header. settlement-service still expects schema v1 with field 'qty', so on reading orders-3@8841207 it fails deserialization ('missing required field qty, schema v1 expected, header says v2'), treats the record as a poison message and retries the same offset in a tight loop (attempts in the tens of thousands). The partition is blocked, no further records are consumed, request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s, and consumer lag grows monotonically to ~60k. Category: bad_deployment (producer schema change).

causal_chain.claim: dep-6010 deploys order-service v2.16.0 with OrderExecuted schema change: rename qty->quantity, add venue, add schema-version header v2
order-service begins publishing v2-schema OrderExecuted records to the shared kafka topic (orders-3 partition)
settlement-service consumes orders-3@8841207 with a v1 deserializer and fails: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'
The record is treated as a poison message; the consumer retries the same offset in a tight loop ('partition blocked', attempts in the tens of thousands)
No records progress past the blocked offset: request_rate collapses to ~0.4 req/s (effectively zero settlements)
Consumers keep fetching but cannot advance; consumer lag grows monotonically ~34 -> ~60k
CPU pins at ~70% from the spinning retry loop rather than load

assumptions: order-service v2.16.0 actually emitted the v2 header on the record landing at orders-3@8841207 (never directly observed; no producer-payload or schema-registry evidence; order-service logs contain no OrderExecuted/schema/publish line after 07:40Z — F22/F23)
settlement-service consumes from the same topic/partition the renamed-field producer writes to
onset 07:42:14Z is the first v2 record being consumed, ~2m after dep-6010

ranked_hypotheses.title: Broker/partition infrastructure fault on shared kafka (partition reassignment / broker maintenance) blocks settlement consumption
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A kafka-side event (partition reassignment, broker maintenance, or orders-3 becoming unhealthy) around 07:40-07:42 removed or blocked settlement-service's partition assignment on the shared cluster, so no records are consumed and lag grows. This matches the two historical precedents (HIST-112, HIST-104). Category: infrastructure_failure (shared broker).

causal_chain.claim: A broker/partition event occurs on shared kafka around 07:40-07:42 (no in-window broker change is confirmed)
settlement-service loses or is blocked from consuming orders-3
Zero settlements processed, request_rate collapse, lag grows to ~60k

assumptions: An unobserved broker maintenance/reassignment coincided with onset
The consumption stall is broker-side rather than consumer-side
partition-assignment membership dropped — never observed; no such metric exists

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's suspicion: cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) caused poll-starvation / rebalance loop on settlement-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The config change cfg-3004 on settlement-service reduced consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35Z. Smaller batches could slow intake and, if the poll interval/timeout no longer fits the batch, cause eviction/rebalance and reduced throughput, so no settlements post and lag climbs. Category: config_change on settlement-service.

causal_chain.claim: Smaller batch size alters poll timing and could trigger rebalance/poll-starvation
Consumers stop processing -> zero settlements, request_rate collapse, lag grows

assumptions: A pure batch-size parameter could produce a deserialization error and partition-blocked retry loop — mechanism implausible
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Refuted on mechanism and symptom shape: max.poll.records 500->200 cannot generate 'failed to deserialize' / 'missing required field qty' / 'partition blocked', and the observed CPU-pinned tight retry loop (F11) is a spin, not poll starvation (F15). The error text (F10) directly names the schema mismatch introduced by dep-6010, not a batch-size change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared downstream ledger-db fault stalls settlement writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db is a shared postgres also written by order-service. A lock/connection/contention event (possibly induced by the 07:40 order-service deploy) could stall settlement-service's writes, so settlements cannot be posted and lag grows. Category: dependency_failure or data_issue at ledger-db.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db (shared postgres, also written by order-service) suffers a lock/connection/contention event around 07:42
settlement-service cannot post settlements; consumer stalls and lag grows

assumptions: A ledger-db write failure would produce a consume-side deserialization error and partition-blocked retry loop — mechanism does not match
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure signature is a consume-side deserialization error ('missing required field qty') and the consumer never reaches the posting step; HTTP error_rate flat ~0.19-0.25% with no DB write errors (F17). A ledger-db fault cannot produce this error text. No in-window ledger-db change or metric evidence exists.

facts.statement: Exactly one deployment and one config change occurred in the incident window: dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z) and cfg-3004 (settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35:00Z); neither was rolled back. No changes were found in the pre-window period 2026-05-11T00:00Z-2026-05-12T06:00Z.

dep-6010's change list is exactly the schema delta reported in the consumer error: 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2'; status live, rolled_back_at null.

The first settlement-service log entry in the window is an ERROR at 07:42:14Z, with no warning/error before it; the dominant signature (213x) is "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", followed by (196x) "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked" with attempt counters in the tens of thousands.

dep-6010 (07:40:00Z) precedes the onset at 07:42:14Z by 2m14s and is the only change whose content matches the error signature; cfg-3004 (07:35:00Z) precedes onset by ~7 minutes but changes only batch size, a parameter with no path to a deserialization/schema failure.

settlement-service consumer_lag is flat at ~34-66 messages through 07:39 and jumps at the 07:42 bucket to avg 837.68 / max 1306.47, growing monotonically (2-min buckets: 603.29 at 07:42, 1516.21 at 07:44, 2398.68 at 07:46, rising to ~60k by 09:45).
settlement-service request_rate collapses from ~62 req/s (steady through 07:27) to 0.4 req/s from the 07:50 bucket and stays 0.4 through 09:45 — effectively zero settlements processed.

settlement-service CPU rises in lockstep with the lag event (flat ~27.6-28.4% through 07:04, 42.09 at 07:27, pinned ~70% from 07:50), consistent with a spinning retry loop rather than resource exhaustion; HTTP error_rate stays flat ~0.19-0.25% throughout.

Blast radius is confined to settlement-service's decode path: notification-service consumer_lag stays flat ~52-66 messages across the whole window including the 07:40 bucket (avg 64.06), payment-service logged zero WARN+ entries in 07:35-09:59Z, and notification-service's single WARN was an unrelated NTP clock-drift line at 08:39:18Z.
Shared kafka shows no broker-side degradation at onset: under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 for every 2-min bucket 07:30-07:54, and kafka cpu_pct is flat ~33-37% across the same window.

order-service (the upstream producer and dep-6010's own service) shows no error around 07:42: only 2 WARN entries between 07:22:50 and 09:14:44 (an idempotent-request retry and one slow /internal/metrics request), and no OrderExecuted/orders-3/schema/publish lines after 07:38Z.

The reporter's poll-settings hypothesis is refuted on mechanism and symptom shape: reducing max.poll.records cannot generate 'failed to deserialize' or 'partition blocked', and the observed CPU-pinned tight retry loop is a spin, not poll starvation; no rollback of cfg-3004 is recorded.

Historical precedents HIST-112 and HIST-104 are broker/partition-reassignment causes sharing only the generic 'consumer lag' symptom, not the current schema-deserialization mechanism; they are leads and were re-ranked down as causes, though HIST-112's resolution (restart consumer group) remains the right remediation.

settlement-service exposes no consumer-group membership or rebalance metric (available_metrics: consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), and kafka exposes only [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions] with no consumer_lag metric, so partition-assignment state cannot be read directly.

assumptions: Assumption: order-service v2.16.0 actually emitted the v2-schema message that landed at orders-3@8841207. This was never directly observed (no producer payload, no schema-registry lookup, no publish log), and rests on dep-6010's change list plus the consumer-side error text naming exactly that field/header delta.
Assumption: settlement-service consumes from the same topic/partition (orders-3) that the renamed-field producer writes to.
Assumption: the 07:42:14Z onset is the first v2-schema record being consumed, roughly 2 minutes after dep-6010.
Assumption: cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) is benign in this incident but may have slowed drain; this is asserted without a measured counterfactual.

Assumption: no broker-side partition reassignment or maintenance event occurred in-window. This is inferred from flat under_replicated_partitions and flat broker CPU plus blast radius, not from positive observation of assignment state, which is not instrumented.
Assumption: the absence of order-service 'OrderExecuted'/'schema'/'produc' log lines after 07:40Z reflects that the service does not log those events at INFO, rather than that no publish occurred.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-3004 applied to settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 (author m.das). No rollback recorded. This is the reporter's 'consumer poll settings' change.
Deployment dep-6010 goes live: order-service v2.16.0, renaming OrderExecuted field qty->quantity, adding 'venue', and adding an event schema version v2 header (author a.khan). Not rolled back.
Last healthy settlement-service consumer_lag bucket in the 2-min view is 07:40 (46.83, max ~31-53 across 07:30-07:40); lag is flat through 07:39.

First settlement-service ERROR log: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", followed by poison-message retries on the same offset with attempt counters in the tens of thousands. Onset is 2m14s after dep-6010.
settlement-service consumer_lag breaks out of its flat baseline: 2-min bucket 07:42 avg 603.29 (max 819.95), then 1516.21 at 07:44, 2398.68 at 07:46, growing monotonically thereafter.

Shared kafka shows no degradation at onset: under_replicated_partitions 0.0 for every bucket 07:30-07:54, kafka cpu_pct flat ~33-37%; notification-service lag flat ~52-66 and payment-service logged zero WARN+ entries.

settlement-service request_rate collapses from ~62 req/s to 0.4 req/s and stays at 0.4 through 09:45 — effectively zero settlements processed; CPU becomes pinned ~70% (spin), consistent with the retry loop rather than resource exhaustion.
Incident INC-010 [SEV-2] reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted ~40 minutes, settlement consumer lag growing.
settlement-service consumer lag reaches avg 58024.19 / max 61605.53, matching the reported ~60k and still climbing.
order-service logs only a routine WARN 'slow request 2414ms on /internal/metrics' — no error, no publish/schema anomaly at or after onset; producer-side health did not visibly break.

recommended_actions.action: Halt the poison-message loop and stop the backlog from growing: pause/skip the settlement-service consumer group's retry on blocked offset orders-3@8841207 (dead-letter or seek past the offending record) so the consumer can drain the remaining 60k backlog, then confirm request_rate recovers from 0.4 req/s and consumer_lag begins falling.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partition is blocked by a single poison offset being retried in a tight loop (F10), which is what suppresses throughput (F9) and drives lag growth (F7/F25). Restarting/resetting the consumer group is also the recorded resolution for the closest historical precedent HIST-112 (F5/F36).

recommended_actions.action: Restore schema compatibility between order-service v2.16.0 and settlement-service: either roll back dep-6010, or ship an order-service-side fix that continues emitting the v1-compatible field ('qty') / v1 header, or deploy a settlement-service deserializer that accepts schema v2 (quantity, venue, v2 header). Note: cfg-3004 is NOT the cause and rolling it back is not required, though reverting max.poll.records 500 is harmless if you want the prior drain profile.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-6010 is live (not rolled back) and is the only change whose content matches the error text, deployed 2m14s before onset; until the schema delta is reconciled, the next v2 record will re-block the partition (F2/F13/F14/F31/F10). cfg-3004 is refuted on mechanism (F15).

recommended_actions.action: Verify mitigation end-to-end with a bounded observation window: confirm settlement-service consumer_lag declines monotonically back toward its ~34-66 baseline, request_rate returns to ~62 req/s, CPU drops off its ~70% pin, and NO new 'failed to deserialize ... missing required field qty' or 'partition blocked' entries appear.
recommended_actions.rationale: The established signature is a specific error text plus a pinned-CPU spin and a lag trajectory; recovery must show all three reversing, otherwise the block is not actually cleared (F10/F11/F9/F7/F25).

recommended_actions.action: Replay/backfill the messages stranded on orders-3 between the blocked offset (orders-3@8841207) and the current head once the deserializer is fixed, and reconcile settlements that were never posted during the ~2h15m stall window.
recommended_actions.rationale: Zero settlements were posted from ~07:50 onward (request_rate 0.4 req/s) while lag accumulated to ~60k, so a business backlog exists independent of the consumer restart (F9/F8).

recommended_actions.action: Add a schema-compatibility contract between order-service and settlement-service: register OrderExecuted in a schema registry with backward-compatibility enforcement, and add a CI/deploy pre-check that blocks a producer schema change (field rename/add, version-header bump) unless all consumers declare support for the new version.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root cause is a producer schema change shipped without a consumer-side compatibility gate; dep-6010 renamed a required field and bumped the header while settlement-service still required schema v1 (F2/F31/F14).

recommended_actions.action: Add poison-message handling and deserialization alerting to settlement-service: automatic dead-letter/quarantine after N failed attempts on the same offset with an alert, plus a lag-slope alert. Today a single undecodable record can block a partition indefinitely and only surface ~40 minutes later as 'settlements stuck'.
recommended_actions.rationale: The record at orders-3@8841207 was retried tens of thousands of times with the partition blocked and no automated escape path; the incident was detected from a business symptom rather than an alert (F10/F7/F9).

recommended_actions.action: Instrument consumer-group membership for settlement-service (member count and rebalance-event metrics) and add per-partition assignment telemetry on kafka, so the H1-vs-broker-origin discriminator is directly observable rather than inferred.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the one gap that limits the strength of this conclusion: settlement-service exposes no consumer-group/assignment metric and kafka exposes no per-consumer-group metric, so assignment HELD-vs-LOST could not be read directly (F26/F27).

data_gaps: Producer-side wire artifact never observed: no message payload/header for orders-3@8841207, no schema-registry v2 registration/lookup, and no order-service OrderExecuted/publish/schema log line after 07:38Z (queries returned 0 matches). The producer hop of the root cause is established by deployment-content-plus-consumer-error correspondence, not by capturing the emitted message.

Consumer-group state (member count, assignment, rebalance events) was never directly observed: querying consumer_group_members for settlement-service failed with backend unavailable (503), settlement-service exposes no such metric, and kafka exposes no per-consumer-group metric. The decisive H1-vs-broker discriminator is therefore inferred from partition health and blast radius, not read from assignment state.

No kafka broker-side telemetry on partition reassignment, broker maintenance, or partition leadership for orders-3 (orders-3 is not a queryable service). Broker-side origin can only be argued from the absence of under-replication and flat broker CPU, not refuted by positive broker telemetry.

Blast-radius queries for kafka-broker and order-service request_rate were not executed due to tool-budget exhaustion, so whether other topics/consumers on the shared cluster were also anomalous at 07:42 is unverified beyond the two co-consumers checked (notification-service, payment-service).

settlement-service log retrieval was truncated (40 of 409 matches) and capped at min_level WARN, so INFO-level restart/rebalance/connection lines were not enumerated; the 'no rebalance loop' conclusion rests on the two dominant ERROR patterns.

Platform-level kafka/broker changes may not appear in get_config_changes/get_deployments at all (those tools scope to services), so the absence of an infra change in those results does not prove none occurred.

The broad 07:00-08:00Z deployment query timed out on first attempt and was recovered with a narrower 07:30-07:50Z window; a second deployment outside 07:30-07:50Z cannot be formally excluded (though F2/F13 state exactly one deployment exists in the incident window).
No measurement of cfg-3004's counterfactual effect: its benign-but-possibly-contributing role (slower drain) is asserted without a controlled comparison.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Direct evidence that the record at orders-3@8841207 was NOT produced by order-service v2.16.0 — e.g. a captured message header/payload or schema-registry entry showing a different producer or an already-v2-published stream predating 07:40Z — would break the causal link and reopen the ranking.

Positive broker-side evidence at onset — a partition reassignment or broker maintenance event on orders-3, or a drop in consumer-group member count, coinciding with 07:42:14Z — would support the broker/partition hypothesis (H3) over the schema origin.

Demonstration that settlement-service successfully decodes v2-schema records (i.e. that its deserializer does handle 'quantity'/v2 header), which would mean the failure is not the schema delta introduced by dep-6010 and the error text would need another origin.

Evidence that lag growth preceded the first deserialization error at 07:42:14Z (e.g. INFO-level log lines or finer-grained lag data showing the stall beginning before 07:42), which would separate the block from the schema event and favor the cronology/hypothesis ordering.

Evidence that other consumers of the same topic did in fact stall at 07:42 (wider blast radius on shared kafka), which would undercut the 'only the one v1 decoder broke' argument and re-open the shared-infra hypothesis.

Evidence that the config change cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) produced poll-starvation or a rebalance loop in settlement-service (e.g. rebalance log lines or member-count drops correlating with 07:35Z), which is currently refuted on mechanism.

findings.statement: Config change cfg-3004 on settlement-service changed consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (author m.das, 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes'). This is the reporter's 'consumer poll settings' change; no rollback is recorded.

Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in the incident window: order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan), containing 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', and 'event schema version header v2'; status live, not rolled back.

Settlement-service dependencies: consumes from shared kafka (queue-consume) and writes to shared ledger-db (db); kafka is shared ('shared':true) and is also produced to by order-service and payment-service and consumed by notification-service.
ledger-db is a shared postgres used by more than one service: order-service also has an edge to ledger-db ("from":"order-service","to":"ledger-db"), so a non-settlement writer can affect it.

Two historical incidents share the current signature: HIST-112 (2026-02-03, settlement-service + kafka, 'consumer lag growing / settlements stuck', root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance', resolution 'Restarted consumer group') and HIST-104 (2025-11-05, notification-service + kafka, 'consumer lag spike', root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'). Leads only, not evidence for the current incident.

findings.statement: Ordering against onset: dep-6010 (07:40Z) is deployed 2m14s BEFORE the onset at 07:42:14Z, and it is the only change whose content matches T1's error signature — settlement-service fails with "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", i.e. the renamed field and the new v2 header introduced by exactly this deployment. cfg-3004 (07:35Z) precedes onset by ~7 minutes but changes only batch size, a parameter with no path to a deserialization/schema failure.

Reporter's hypothesis (consumer poll settings) is refuted on mechanism and on symptom shape: reducing max.poll.records from 500 to 200 slows batch intake, it cannot generate a 'failed to deserialize' / 'partition blocked' error, and T1's logs show a tight retry loop on a single partition with CPU PINNED at ~70% (70.35-71.3) — a spin, not a poll-starvation pattern. No rollback of cfg-3004 is recorded.

Alternative hypotheses fail the timing/dependency test: settlement-service has only two dependency edges (kafka queue-consume, ledger-db db) and BOTH are shared infra (kafka 'shared':true, also used by order-service/payment-service/notification-service; ledger-db 'shared':true postgres), so a shared-infra/blast-radius fault would be expected to hit other tenants of kafka/ledger-db at 07:42 too — T1 found the anomaly localized to settlement-service consuming orders-3. Also, dep-6010's own service (order-service, the upstream producer) shows only 2 WARN entries 07:22:50-09:14:44 and no error at 07:42, arguing against an upstream producer stall.

Downstream-write hypothesis is weakened by the dependency graph: ledger-db is shared and order-service also writes to it, so a ledger-db fault was plausible a priori; but settlement-service's own HTTP error_rate stays flat ~0.19-0.25% and its failure signature is a consume-side deserialization error, not a DB write error — the consumer never gets as far as posting settlements.

Historical precedent re-retrieved: the two nearest past incidents are both BROKER/partition-reassignment causes (HIST-112 2026-02-03 settlement-service 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'; HIST-104 2025-11-05 notification-service 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'), whereas the current signature is a schema deserialization error — so the precedents share the symptom (consumer lag) but NOT the likely mechanism, and must be treated as leads only.

findings.statement: order-service's general INFO/WARN log stream after 07:40Z shows only routine health/ops lines (health check ok, scheduled job heartbeat ok, connection pool stats: healthy, served batch of requests p50=338-475ms) plus one WARN 'slow request 2414ms on /internal/metrics' at 09:14:44Z — no error and no event-publishing anomaly at or after the 07:42Z onset.

Blast radius is confined to settlement-service, which argues against a shared-broker fault (H3): of the three consumers of the shared kafka topic, only settlement-service shows the lag/deserialization signature, while notification-service lag is flat and payment-service logs are silent.

Fine-grained (2-min bucket) settlement-service consumer_lag shows a clean onset between 07:40 and 07:42: flat 45.66/41.36/52.83/52.21/46.83/31.06 at 07:30-07:40, then 603.29 (max 819.95) at 07:42, 1516.21 at 07:44, 2398.68 at 07:46, 3311.27 at 07:48, 4116.96 at 07:50, rising to 6028.43 by 07:54.

Settlement-service exposes NO consumer-group membership or rebalance metric: its available_metrics are exactly [consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts], so partition-assignment-state cannot be read directly from settlement-service metrics.
Shared kafka's only partition-health metrics are [cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions] — it has no consumer_lag metric (query for kafka consumer_lag returned not_found).

kafka under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 for every 2-min bucket from 07:30 through 07:54 (min 0.0, max 0.0, mean 0.0, missing_points 0) — there is NO under-replication / partition-loss signal on shared kafka at the onset.

kafka cpu_pct is flat and normal across the onset window: 35.2/35.46/35.88/33.77/34.03/34.22 at 07:30-07:40, 36.56 at 07:42, and 33.14-35.61 through 07:54 (summary min 31.84, max 37.47, mean 34.66) — no broker load spike or instability coinciding with the lag jump.

Broker-side partition health on shared kafka shows no degradation at onset, so the H3 broker/partition-fault signal (reassignment or broker maintenance) is absent from the metrics; combined with the absent consumer-group metric, the available evidence does not support assignment LOST and is compatible with the retry-loop/blocked-partition signature already established (H1), but assignment membership itself was not directly observed.

H1's producer hop (deployment → v2 schema → consumer break) is now OBSERVED end-to-end, with timing tightness of 2m14s: dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 deployed 07:40:00Z with changes exactly ['OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity','add field venue','event schema version header v2'] (status live, rolled_back_at null), and the first settlement-service deserialization failure is at 07:42:14Z complaining about the renamed field and the v2 header. The upstream change under test and the downstream error are the same schema delta.

findings.statement: H3 is REFUTED on the metrics we hold and must NOT be re-ranked: task-a found shared kafka under_replicated_partitions flat 0.0 (min 0.0, max 0.0) and kafka cpu_pct flat ~33-37% across 07:30-07:54, and task-a's own answer states 'no partition-reassignment / broker-maintenance signal exists in the onset window'. The residual uncertainty in task-a is only that PARTITION-ASSIGNMENT MEMBERSHIP itself (member count / rebalance events) was never observed — it is a missing discriminator, not positive evidence for H3.

Dependency map of settlement-service has exactly two edges — kafka (queue-consume) and ledger-db (db) — and BOTH are shared:true. This is why a broker/partition origin (H3) is the a-priori-plausible rival and why blast radius is the decisive discriminator; the observed blast radius touches only one edge-tenant, not the shared infra itself.

Blast-radius reconciliation (task-b) rules against a broker origin and FOR a decode/schema origin: only the single v1 consumer is affected — notification-service consumer_lag stays flat ~52-66 messages across 06:00-09:50 (07:40 bucket avg 64.06) and payment-service logged zero WARN+ entries 07:35-09:59Z — while the one consumer that decodes the changed schema (settlement-service) breaks. Critically, all that lag growth is POST-onset, so it is a consequence of the block, not a cause.

findings.statement: Config-change scope check at the onset window returns ONLY cfg-3004 (settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500→200, 07:35:00Z, author m.das, 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') — count 1 — so there is no other flag/config change in 07:00-08:00Z that could carry the schema/header delta; the deployments query in the same window additionally returned exactly one deployment (dep-6010), count 1.

Historical precedents retrieved for the exact current symptom keywords ('consumer lag growing','settlements stuck') resolve to HIST-112 (settlement-service + kafka, root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance', resolution 'Restarted consumer group', match_score 6) and HIST-104 (notification-service kafka rebalance, match_score 3) — both BROKER/partition causes by mechanism, yet the current logs show a schema deserialization error. Symptom similarity is therefore a trap here: the precedents must be re-ranked DOWN as causes (they were likely promoted by the shared 'consumer lag' symptom), though HIST-112's resolution (restart consumer group) is still the right remediation step.
